58e4ea54ebf0: Have the student name one sign per row that they have seen in Poland or back home. Explain the triangle and the octagon shapes as «so you recognise them even from behind».
3c6790c4db82: English has a similar pattern (overtake → overtaking), but Polish more often gives -anie/-enie. Ask for two more: hamować → hamowanie, cofać → cofanie.
e2658b7891ce: A bridge back to lesson 1: the student already knows «Proszę zawrócić». Now the same action as the name of a sign: «zakaz zawracania».
bc06d02750e4: A pedestrian stepping onto a crossing has priority as of 1 June 2021 (art. 13 ust. 1a, art. 26 PoRD). A tram at an equal-priority intersection — art. 25. Don't go deep into traffic lights — those come in later lessons.
8e56768a6180: Does this sign mean «no stopping»? — YES / NO
e36e82a4ecd4: Answers: 1 — depends on the picture (ask what the sign looks like); 2 — yes, at an equal-priority crossroads; 3 — yes. Revise the structures from lesson 1: masz obowiązek, powinieneś.
8a9af76110e3: Show road signs on your phone (search «znaki drogowe B»); the student answers using the formula.
d2454820cac0: Zakaz postoju ≠ zakaz zatrzymywania się: under the first you may stop for a minute, under the second you may not. A frequent test question.
c362fedd3548: To overtake = wyprzedzać. „Obgon” does not exist in Polish.
7396378b41bb: «Ustąpić drogi» does occur in speech, but on the test and on the road sign it is only pierwszeństwa.
